statement: In adults who smoked cigarettes and joined randomised trials (11 trials, 7,214 people; Cochrane living review, searched to 1 January 2026), being given a nicotine vape, compared with behavioural support only or no support, was followed by more people not smoking at 6 months or longer: about 4 more in 100 (9 against 5 in 100, interval 7 to 11; risk ratio 1.75, 95% CI 1.39 to 2.20; I² 13%; analysed as allocated, with people lost to follow-up counted as smoking). The 5 in 100 is the review's assumed quit rate with limited support, not the trials' observed rate. The review rates this low certainty, because the trials could not be blinded and the vape groups had more support than the comparison groups, so part of the gap may come from the extra support rather than the vape; its funnel plot is also asymmetric. Leaving out the one industry-funded trial (JUUL Labs) gave 1.53 (1.30 to 1.79). Being advised to use a vape without being given one showed no clear difference from no such advice (risk ratio 1.02, 0.88 to 1.19; 2 trials, 2,652 people; not graded by the review). Follow-up for quitting was 6 months or longer, all participants were adults, and the review says longer-term effects are unknown. Certainty: low. Status: replicated.
plain: When adults who smoked were given a vape with nicotine, more of them were not smoking 6 months or more later than adults given counselling only or nothing: about 9 in 100 against 5 in 100. But the trials could not hide who got the vape, and the vape groups usually got more support too, so the real gap could be smaller. Advising people to vape, without giving them a vape, made no clear difference.
population: Adults who smoked cigarettes and joined randomised trials of nicotine vapes in which the comparison group got behavioural support only or no support (11 trials, 7,214 people; Cochrane living review, search to 1 January 2026); two further trials of advice to use a vape (2,652 people)
exposure: Being given a nicotine vape (refillable in five trials, cartridge in three, pod in three), alone or with the trial's support
comparator: Behavioural support only, or no support (brief advice or nothing)
outcome: Not smoking at 6 months or longer (strictest definition, biochemically confirmed where possible, people lost to follow-up counted as smoking)
magnitude: Cessation at 6+ months vs behavioural support only or no support: RR 1.75 (95% CI 1.39–2.20), I² 13%, 11 trials, 7,214 participants; 5 per 100 (assumed) vs 9 per 100 (7–11), about 4 more in 100 (2–6), editors' subtraction; low certainty. Without the industry-funded trial (Xu 2023) 1.53 (1.30–1.79). Advice to use a vape without supplying one vs no advice: RR 1.02 (0.88–1.19), I² 0%, 2 trials, 2,652 participants; unchanged without the high-risk trial; not graded.

evidence.locator: Results › Synthesis of results › Cessation › Versus behavioural support or no support, 1st and 2nd paragraphs; Table 2 (Analysis 9.1); Summary of findings 3
evidence.extracted: Nicotine vape against behavioural support only or no support, abstinence at six months or longer: RR 1.75 (1.39 to 2.20), I² 13%, 11 trials (five refillable, three cartridge, three pod), 7,214 participants; 5 per 100 (assumed) against 9 per 100 (7 to 11), about 4 more in 100 (interval 2 to 6; editors' subtraction). Low certainty: two levels for risk of bias because blinding was not possible and levels of support differed between arms. One trial was industry-funded (Xu 2023, JUUL Labs); without it RR 1.53 (1.30 to 1.79). One trial (Pulvers 2020) could not be pooled.

evidence.locator: Results › Risk of bias in included studies; Summary of findings 3 footnote a; Results › Reporting biases; Discussion › Limitations of the evidence included in the review, 3rd paragraph
evidence.extracted: Across the 80 trials (RoB 1): 12 low risk of bias, 27 unclear, 41 high; performance bias high in 24. The summary-of-findings footnote gives lack of blinding and differential support between arms as the reason for the two-level downgrade. The funnel plot for the behavioural-support cessation pool (11 trials) shows some asymmetry; the authors say plots with this few studies are not diagnostic and did not downgrade for publication bias.

evidence.locator: Results › Synthesis of results › Advice to use EC to stop smoking, 1st and 2nd paragraphs; Table 1 (Vickerman 2022 row)
evidence.extracted: Advice to use a vape without being given one, against no such advice: RR 1.02 (0.88 to 1.19), I² 0%, 2 trials (Martinez 2021, low risk of bias, in people who already vaped; Elling 2023, high risk), 2,652 participants; no clear difference, and the interpretation was unchanged without Elling 2023. A third trial (Vickerman 2022; 110 randomised, 52 in the adverse-event analyses) reported more adverse events with the advice, but the interval included no difference (RR 1.27, 0.72 to 2.26), and no serious events. None industry-funded.

evidence.extracted: Authors: longer-term health effects are unknown and the review includes safety data to two years only; the trials tested regulated nicotine vapes; unpublished data may be missing; all trials were in adults; the search ran to 1 January 2026.

risk_of_bias.note: Lack of blinding and differential support between arms (the review's rating).

grade.reasoning: Randomised evidence, starting high, read through a Cochrane living review (AMSTAR 2: high confidence, on the study card). Risk of bias, two levels, as the review rates it: the trials could not be blinded and the vape groups received more support than the comparison groups, so some of the difference may come from the extra contact rather than the vape; of the 80 trials in the review 41 were at high risk of bias, and the one trial in this pool with low risk overall gives only a very imprecise result on its own. Inconsistency, not rated down (I² 13%). Indirectness, not rated down: the claim is limited to adults in trials where the vape was supplied. Imprecision, not rated down: 7,214 people and an interval from 1.39 to 2.20. Publication bias, not rated down: the pool's funnel plot is asymmetric (11 trials; the authors say not diagnostic), which the editors do not count as a further level because small unblinded trials that favour the vape are the same worry as the risk-of-bias rating; counting it would give very low. The result holds without the one industry-funded trial (JUUL Labs). The advice-only comparison is not graded by the review; it rests on two trials (one in people who already vaped, one high risk) and its interval (0.88 to 1.19) allows both a modest benefit and a modest harm, so it supports no more than no clear difference. Status replicated: 11 trials by different groups give the same direction with little heterogeneity; the review is a living review and later updates will change the numbers.

verification.flag_note: Staged apart from cl_nic_vapes_stopping so that the weaker comparison keeps its own rating (low, as Cochrane gives it). Relation is-associated-with (not a causal verb) because the certainty is low and the arms differed in support. The advice-only result is placed here because its comparator is no advice; the review does not grade it. The 5 in 100 baseline is an assumed rate. The funnel asymmetry is noted but not counted as an extra level (see the grade reasoning): a stricter reading would be very low. Not read: supplementary materials, forest and funnel figures, trial reports. Living review: re-check at the next update.
